sentences.zh: 但数量并不大。

sentences.zh: 事实上，他为此进行了大力游说，以至于斯大林曾开玩笑说，米高扬一定比爱共产主义更爱冰淇淋。

sentences.en: The Soviet Union's first ice cream factory reached a total volume of 46,000 tons of ice cream a year.
sentences.zh: 苏联第一家冰淇淋工厂的年产量达到了46,000吨。

sentences.en: Under Mikhayan's leadership, a completely new culture around ice cream started to form.
sentences.zh: 在米高扬的领导下，一种全新的冰淇淋文化开始形成。

sentences.en: All ice cream vendors wore special uniforms, white caps, aprons, and overcoats.
sentences.zh: 所有的冰淇淋小贩都穿着特殊的制服，戴着白帽子，系着围裙，穿着大衣。

sentences.en: People would go out in the dead of winter and hang around just eating ice cream in their winter jackets.

sentences.zh: 然后它接着说，在口味和质量方面，

sentences.zh: 食品工业生产的冰淇淋总是优于家庭自制的冰淇淋。

sentences.zh: 就像是，这里有几个食谱，

sentences.zh: 但别费心去尝试了。

sentences.en: And maybe that was the whole point.
sentences.zh: 也许这才是重点所在。

sentences.en: The book was a cookbook, yeah,
sentences.zh: 这本书是一本食谱，没错，

sentences.en: but having people make its recipes wasn't the goal.
sentences.zh: 但让人们制作书中的食谱并不是目的。

sentences.en: More so, it was meant to show you what was worth desiring,
sentences.zh: 更重要的是，它旨在向你展示什么是值得渴望的，

sentences.en: and that socialism would get you there eventually.
sentences.zh: 并且社会主义最终会让你实现这些渴望。

sentences.en: But the truth was much more grim.
sentences.zh: 但事实却要严峻得多。

sentences.en: In fact, most of Babushka's memories
sentences.zh: 事实上，奶奶的大部分记忆

sentences.en: are not of lavish spreads and homemade desserts,
sentences.zh: 并不是关于丰盛的宴席和自制甜点，

sentences.zh: 而是关于食物的匮乏。

sentences.en: Here's Mark again, translating Babushka's Russian.
sentences.zh: 这是马克，正在翻译奶奶的俄语。

sentences.zh: 奶奶一直有一种喂养他人的冲动。

sentences.en: But when she was a child, it was tough for her mom to watch Babushka give away food,
sentences.zh: 但当她还是个孩子的时候，看着奶奶把食物分给别人，她妈妈很难过，

sentences.en: because they didn't have much at all.
sentences.zh: 因为他们自己根本没有多少东西。

sentences.zh: 她说她小时候生病时，妈妈会给她煮鸡汤，

sentences.zh: 外面院子里或者房子周围总有男孩，

sentences.zh: 她会隔着窗户用勺子喂他们。

sentences.zh: 张着嘴？

sentences.zh: 是的！

sentences.zh: 就像小海鸥一样。

sentences.zh: 这些故事现在听起来很有趣，

sentences.en: but that kind of hunger,
sentences.zh: 但那种饥饿感，

sentences.en: Babushka says,
sentences.zh: 奶奶说，

sentences.en: it's difficult for us kids to imagine.
sentences.zh: 我们这些孩子很难想象。

sentences.en: It's impossible to imagine.
sentences.zh: 简直无法想象。

sentences.en: And I wish for you never to know that and never to see it.
sentences.zh: 我希望你们永远不要经历，也永远不要看到那种景象。

sentences.en: It is hard to imagine, especially as I flip through pages of the book.
sentences.zh: 这确实很难想象，尤其是当我翻阅这本书的时候。

sentences.en: Because even as Mikayan was implementing his cuisine and revising this cookbook,
sentences.zh: 因为即使在米高扬推行他的烹饪法并修订这本食谱时，

sentences.en: and certain foods were indeed taking off,
sentences.zh: 某些食物确实流行了起来，

sentences.en: his successes were papering over a dark underlying reality.
sentences.zh: 但他的成功掩盖了一个黑暗的潜在现实。

sentences.en: But hunger was still the primary struggle.
sentences.zh: 饥饿仍然是主要的问题。

sentences.en: Because it turns out many of the foods that Miki-Yan's factories were churning out day after day
sentences.zh: 因为事实证明，米高扬的工厂日复一日生产的许多食物，

sentences.en: were rarely ever available for purchase.
sentences.zh: 很少能在商店里买到。

sentences.en: Even though everyone knew about these foods, the grocery shelves were mostly empty.
sentences.zh: 尽管每个人都知道这些食物，但杂货店的货架大多是空的。

sentences.en: For decades, outside of a handful of stores in the big cities,
sentences.zh: 几十年来，除了大城市里的少数几家商店外，

sentences.en: there weren't many places you could just plunk down your rubles and buy this stuff.
sentences.zh: 没有多少地方能让你掏出卢布买到这些东西。

sentences.en: Most of the food, it turned out, had been disappearing into networks of privileged elites
sentences.zh: 事实证明，大部分食物在到达货架之前，

sentences.en: long before it even reached the shelves.
sentences.zh: 就已经消失在特权精英的网络中了。

sentences.en: Everyone tried to befriend a butcher.
sentences.zh: 每个人都试图和屠夫搞好关系。

sentences.en: You'd smile extra hard as you walked in the store.
sentences.zh: 你走进商店时会笑得格外灿烂。

sentences.en: You had to, if you had any hope of getting a good piece of meat, or any meat at all.
sentences.zh: 如果你想买到一块好肉，或者哪怕是任何肉，你都必须这样做。

sentences.en: Yeah, I mean, food was the object of, you know, constant longing, desire, anxiety.
sentences.zh: 是的，我的意思是，食物是人们不断渴望、向往和焦虑的对象。

sentences.en: It was really pretty much the focus of our lives.
sentences.zh: 它几乎是我们生活的重心。

sentences.en: Like, you know, I literally had a banana maybe like four times in my life.
sentences.zh: 就像，我这辈子可能只吃过四次香蕉。

sentences.en: Because food supply was unpredictable,
sentences.zh: 因为食物供应不可预测，

sentences.en: Anya told me that anytime she left the house,
sentences.zh: 安雅告诉我，每次她出门，

sentences.zh: 口袋里都会塞着一个揉成一团的网兜。

sentences.en: The bag was called a vojska, which means what if.
sentences.zh: 这个袋子叫“万一袋”，意思是“万一呢”。

sentences.en: As in, what if I stumble upon a store with food inside it today?
sentences.zh: 意思是，万一我今天偶然发现一家有食物的商店呢？

sentences.en: So there was this kind of chase, the unpredictability.
sentences.zh: 所以这是一种追逐，一种不可预测性。

sentences.en: Oh, you know, you pass a store and there's a long line for something.
sentences.zh: 哦，你路过一家商店，看到那里排着长队买东西。

sentences.en: Some people just would get into the line without even asking what it was for.
sentences.zh: 有些人甚至连问都不问是什么，就直接排进去了。

sentences.en: Meanwhile, at home, the book offered salivating images of the kind of food you were supposed to be able to eat.
sentences.zh: 与此同时，在家里，这本书提供了令人垂涎的食物图片，让你觉得那是你应该能吃到的。

sentences.en: So we looked at those pictures, you know, I think there's one picture of, you know, suckling pig.
sentences.zh: 所以我们看着那些照片，我想有一张烤乳猪的照片，

sentences.en: And there's one picture of oysters.
sentences.zh: 还有一张牡蛎的照片。

sentences.en: And it's kind of like, OK, we've never seen it.
sentences.zh: 感觉就像是，好吧，我们从来没见过这些东西。

sentences.en: We don't know what this is.
sentences.zh: 我们不知道这是什么。

sentences.en: But, you know, it was advertised.
sentences.zh: 但是，你知道，它被宣传出来了。

sentences.en: Every cookbook sells a fantasy, of course.
sentences.zh: 当然，每一本食谱都在兜售一种幻想。

sentences.en: But it's the discrepancy between the abundance on the pages and the absence in the shops that makes the book so jarring.
sentences.zh: 但正是书页上的富足与商店里的匮乏之间的巨大反差，才让这本书显得如此刺眼。

sentences.en: The book suggested everyone adopt a four-course lunch, but much of the population would batch cook for the week with whatever few ingredients they had on hand.
sentences.zh: 书中建议每个人都采用四道菜的午餐，但大部分人只能用手头仅有的几种食材凑合着做一周的饭。

sentences.en: It's clear who the book was written for.
sentences.zh: 很明显，这本书是为谁写的。

sentences.en: To the Soviet housewife, it reads, in bold typeface on page one.
sentences.zh: 第一页的粗体字写着：致苏联家庭主妇。

sentences.en: But for many Soviet women, the book often lived on a shelf, somewhere out of reach.
sentences.zh: 但对于许多苏联女性来说，这本书通常只是放在书架上，遥不可及。

sentences.en: Back in Babushka's apartment, I wanted to try cooking something from the book together.
sentences.zh: 回到奶奶的公寓，我想一起尝试做书里的一道菜。

sentences.en: I was curious how these recipes held up.
sentences.zh: 我很好奇这些食谱是否经得起考验。

sentences.en: That was good.
sentences.zh: 那很好吃。

sentences.en: The first couple are always throwaways.
sentences.zh: 头几次尝试总是会失败的。

sentences.en: We were trying to make blin, a thin Russian pancake made with leavened wheat batter.
sentences.zh: 我们当时在尝试做布林饼，这是一种用发酵小麦面糊做的俄式薄饼。

sentences.en: Best, you see what, blin, little, little, little, kind of hole.
sentences.zh: 你看，布林饼，这里有个小洞，小小的，小小的。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是啊。

sentences.zh: 你能看透过去吗？

sentences.zh: 能，是的。

sentences.en: They're so thin that you can see through them?
sentences.zh: 它们薄到能看透过去？

sentences.zh: 是啊，我们还没完全掌握要领。

sentences.en: The book's recipes have incredibly vague instructions.
sentences.zh: 这本书里的食谱说明极其模糊。

sentences.zh: 说明就像是写着：把肉放进烤箱直到煮熟，然后上菜。

sentences.en: There are no meal preparation times, no serving sizes.
sentences.zh: 没有烹饪时间，也没有份量说明。

sentences.en: The most frequent instruction in the book is to open a tin can of some kind.
sentences.zh: 书中最常见的指令就是打开某种罐头。

sentences.en: As I mixed the batter together, Babushka flipped through the book, and I peered over her shoulder.
sentences.zh: 当我搅拌面糊时，巴布什卡翻阅着书，我凑到她肩头看。

sentences.en: We landed on a couple recipes that caused her to chuckle.
sentences.zh: 我们翻到了几个让她忍俊不禁的食谱。

sentences.en: Recipes she thinks no one would have followed.
sentences.zh: 她认为根本没人会照着做的食谱。

sentences.en: Meals that called for real crab meat, or fresh figs, or game birds.
sentences.zh: 那些需要用到真蟹肉、新鲜无花果或野禽的菜肴。

sentences.en: It all made me think that this cookbook was useless.
sentences.zh: 这一切让我觉得这本食谱毫无用处。

sentences.en: But Anya told me the book, despite its flaws, did have its uses.
sentences.zh: 但安雅告诉我，尽管有缺陷，这本书确实有它的用途。

sentences.en: Anya remembers noticing how the copies of the book she saw in other people's homes would be heavily annotated.
sentences.zh: 安雅记得她注意到，在别人家里看到的这本书，上面总是密密麻麻地写满了批注。

sentences.en: People would write over the recipes or write in the margins.
sentences.zh: 人们会在食谱上覆盖书写，或者在页边空白处写字。

sentences.en: It became a way of taking the kitchen back, taking something that was produced by the Soviet Union and making it your own.
sentences.zh: 这成了一种夺回厨房主权的方式，把苏联生产的东西变成属于你自己的东西。
